learn.title: Understanding Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)
learn.intro: How do we fund massive wind and solar farms? Without a guaranteed way to sell electricity, developers face too much risk. Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) act as the financial backbone of the green transition, providing the certainty needed to unlock billions in investment for renewable infrastructure worldwide.
learn.c1_text: Think of a PPA as a long-term contract between a seller and a buyer. It is like a subscription service for electricity. A developer agrees to build a plant, and a buyer agrees to buy the power at a fixed price for 10-25 years, ensuring steady revenue to pay back construction loans.
learn.c2_text: Corporations are increasingly using PPAs to meet sustainability goals. By signing these contracts, companies move beyond buying 'green certificates' and instead fund new renewable capacity directly, creating a direct link between corporate demand and actual new solar or wind installations on the grid.
learn.c3_text: In large emerging markets, PPAs help stabilize energy prices. By locking in rates, countries can protect their economies from the volatility of fossil fuel markets, making renewable energy a strategic tool for long-term economic and energy security.
learn.stat1: PPAs drive trillions in renewable investment globally
learn.stat3: Corporate demand is a key driver of new capacity
learn.stat4: Fixed pricing reduces long-term energy volatility

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Earth's Natural Heat
learn.intro: Unlike solar or wind, geothermal energy is 'always on.' By tapping into the intense heat beneath our feet, we can create a constant, reliable source of baseload power that doesn't depend on weather conditions, making it a vital pillar for a stable, carbon-free grid.
learn.c1_text: Imagine the Earth as a giant thermos of hot water. We drill deep wells to reach hot water or steam. This steam travels up to the surface, much like steam from a boiling kettle, to spin a turbine and generate electricity.
learn.c2_text: Geothermal isn't just for electricity. We can use the warm water directly for heating buildings or greenhouses. It is like having a natural radiator under your feet, providing consistent thermal energy with a very small physical footprint compared to other power plants.
learn.c3_text: While highly abundant in volcanic regions, geothermal technology is evolving. New enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) aim to unlock heat anywhere, potentially transforming how we approach heating and power in diverse geographic locations worldwide.
learn.stat4: High capacity factor compared to variable RE

learn.title: Offshore Wind Farm Engineering
learn.intro: Offshore wind captures stronger, more consistent breezes found over the ocean. While more complex to build than onshore farms, these massive installations offer the scale needed to power entire coastal cities and drive the next wave of renewable expansion.
learn.c1_text: Building in the ocean is like building a skyscraper on a moving floor. Engineers use massive steel foundations, either fixed to the seabed or floating on platforms, to keep the turbines steady against waves, currents, and powerful oceanic winds.
learn.c2_text: Getting power from the middle of the sea to the shore is a feat of engineering. It requires specialized subsea cables and offshore substations to step up the voltage, ensuring the electricity can travel long distances without losing significant energy.
learn.c3_text: As offshore wind matures, costs are plummeting. This is enabling massive projects in the North Sea and emerging markets, turning coastal regions into massive renewable energy hubs that can support heavy industrial demand.
learn.stat1: Higher wind speeds than onshore sites

learn.title: India's ISTS Waiver Policy
learn.intro: In a vast country like India, the best renewable resources are often far from the biggest cities. The Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) waiver was a brilliant policy tool designed to bridge this gap and accelerate the green transition.
learn.c1_text: Think of ISTS waivers as a 'toll discount' for green energy. Usually, moving electricity across state lines incurs transmission fees. By waiving these for certain RE projects, the government makes renewable energy much cheaper for buyers in distant states.
learn.c2_text: India has massive solar potential in sunny, arid states like Rajasthan. The policy encourages developers to build there and sell to high-demand states like Maharashtra, ensuring that the best renewable resources are utilized efficiently across the national grid.
learn.c3_text: This policy has been instrumental in India's rapid solar expansion. By reducing the total cost of electricity, it has helped India achieve some of the lowest renewable energy tariffs in the world, making the transition economically irresistible.

learn.title: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV)
learn.intro: Why just put solar panels on a roof when the building itself can be the power plant? BIPV turns entire building surfaces—windows, facades, and roofs—into active energy generators, merging aesthetics with high-performance sustainable architecture.
learn.c1_text: Instead of mounting heavy panels on top of a structure, BIPV replaces traditional materials. It is like a smartphone screen that also acts as a solar charger; the glass itself is the energy collector, making the building look sleek and modern.
learn.c2_text: BIPV components serve two purposes: they provide structural integrity (like a roof or wall) and generate electricity. This reduces the 'embodied carbon' of the building because you are buying one material that does two jobs at once.
learn.c3_text: In dense cities, roof space is limited. BIPV allows skyscrapers to utilize their vast vertical surface areas (facades) to capture sunlight, turning concrete jungles into productive, self-sustaining energy landscapes.

learn.title: How Solar PV Works
learn.intro: Solar panels are essentially magic mirrors for light. By understanding the physics of the photoelectric effect, we can see how a simple beam of sunlight can be converted into the electricity that powers our lives.
learn.c1_text: Imagine sunlight as a stream of tiny ping-pong balls called photons. When these photons hit a solar cell, they knock electrons loose from their atoms. It is like a game of billiards where the white ball hits the colored ones.
learn.c2_text: Inside the solar cell, there is an internal electric field. Once the photons knock the electrons loose, this field forces them to flow in one direction. This organized flow of electrons is exactly what electricity is!
learn.c3_text: The electricity from panels is Direct Current (DC). Since most homes use Alternating Current (AC), we use an inverter to convert it. This is the final step in turning sunlight into usable power for your appliances.
learn.stat3: Requires an inverter for AC power
